• 2026-11-21

    Hacked target: Chainflip

    Description of the event: Cross-chain swap protocol Chainflip was attacked on November 21, 2026. The attacker, through a suspected compromise of the aggregate signing key, drained 122.86 BTC, 520.22 ETH, approximately 3.25 million USDC and 758K USDT from its Bitcoin and Ethereum vaults, totaling about $12 million. Some ETH proceeds were quickly sent to Tornado Cash. The project entered full safe mode (disabling deposits, withdrawals and swaps) and offered the attacker a 10% bounty in exchange for returning 90% of the funds.

    Amount of loss: $ 12,000,000 Attack method: Private Key Leak

  • 2026-11-18

    Hacked target: K3 Capital

    Description of the event: On November 18, 2026, K3 Capital’s sBOLD vault (a yield-bearing ERC-4626 vault built on Liquity V2 Stability Pools) was exploited. Attackers used flash-loaned wstETH to self-liquidate Liquity V2 troves, manipulated the vault’s share accounting (flaw in totalAssets calculation), minted cheap sBOLD shares, swapped collateral, and redeemed other depositors’ BOLD, draining approximately $3.43 million. The team paused the contracts and is investigating.

    Amount of loss: $ 3,430,000 Attack method: Smart Contract Vulnerability

    View Reference Sources

  • 2026-11-18

    Hacked target: Peapods Finance

    Description of the event: On November 18, 2026, Peapods Finance’s deployer private key was apparently compromised. The attacker used it to set a minter on L2 PEAS contracts, mint tokens, bridge them to Ethereum mainnet, and sell them, creating sell pressure. The team quickly withdrew 98-99% of L2 liquidity to limit further extraction and is working on a post-mortem and fund recovery. PEAS cannot be minted on mainnet—only previously bridged tokens could be extracted.

    Amount of loss: - Attack method: Private Key Leakage

    View Reference Sources

  • 2026-11-12

    Hacked target: PennysiaSettlement

    Description of the event: PennysiaSettlement (Ethereum) was exploited via an arbitrary external call vulnerability in executeSwap. The attacker deployed fake tokens to bypass spend checks and used residual user approvals to drain approximately $5,131 in assets from 4 users via transferFrom calls through the settlement contract.

    Amount of loss: $ 5,131 Attack method: Smart Contract Vulnerability
